docSummary: Agency X material describes a single AMS tower covering 12 eServices (Portal, Callup, Manning, Deferment, Payslip, Registration, Clearance, Pay, Awards, Leave and Claims, Retail, Posting) with FY25 (April 2025–31 March 2026, 12 months) ticket data. Raw FY25 totals: SRs=3066, Sev A=155, Sev B=474, Sev C=7, CRs=202; mapping Sev A→P1, Sev B→P2, Sev C→P3 (no P4 category reported) and dividing by 12 months gives inc≈53.0/month (P1=24.37%, P2=74.53%, P3=1.10%, P4=0%), sr≈255.5/month, cr≈16.83/month. L1 is explicitly out of the vendor's scope (agency help desk), with a client-run L1.5 team filtering 20-30% of tickets before L2; of the remainder, less than 5% escalate to L3 (used as pass23≈5%). Two separate automation opportunities were discussed (manual account-review collation, manual weekly log review), both pre-commercial. Several figures look internally inconsistent (Sev A conflict between sessions, Manning data flagged as only six months, Booklet eService missing from the final table, conflicting user counts) and are flagged in warnings rather than silently corrected.

warnings: Conflict: an earlier session reported platform-wide Sev A as 6 for FY25, but the session-4 table totals Sev A at 155 - verify which figure is correct.
Session 3 states '12 eServices in total; one (Booklet) is being decommissioned' but the FY25 table in session 4 lists 12 named eServices with no 'Booklet' row - verify composition/count.
Job Failures (Pay=30, Awards=8, Retail=54, Posting=0, total=92) are operational counters, not described as logged incidents, and were excluded from inc/mix.
Manning row is flagged as only six months of data ('obtain six-month manning data to set the year-one baseline as a full 12 months'); the FY25 total may understate Manning's true annual volume.

Suspect ratios in the FY25 table: Callup shows 140 Sev-A incidents against only 80 SRs; Leave and Claims shows 1600 SRs but only 10 CRs; Retail shows 890 SRs, 1 CR and 54 job failures - verify these against source.

L1 is out of scope for the vendor (agency help desk); an intermediate client-run L1.5 team (3-4 FTE, 24x7) filters 20-30% of tickets - its rate is context only, not used as pass12 since L1 is not in vendor scope.
Conflicting user counts: 'Fewer than 1000 users are supported' (ops model) vs '4000 concurrent users at maximum' (governance) - mau field omitted pending clarification.
Platform team (18 FTE) and infrastructure (public cloud in Singapore, run by a separate hosting vendor) are out of scope for this engagement and were not sized as a tower.
Security incidents are handled by a separate enterprise team and are out of scope - not included in tower volumes.
No statement was found on where the bidder's delivery team is/will be located; Singapore is only the hosting/cloud region, so eng.region/locMix were omitted.
CR complexity (crMix) is not quantified anywhere in the document beyond qualitative notes on policy-driven changes and vendor estimation delays - omitted.
eng.incumbentFTE uses the midpoint (33) of the stated range '30 to 36 people'.
Page 5 content is explicitly an AI-generated/bid-team analysis (indicative pods, FTE estimate) and was excluded from extraction per instructions.
towers.0.coverage ('8x5') is inferred from the generic phrase 'Support hours = business hours' - exact daily hours are not specified; verify.
mix.P4 was assumed to be 0% because only three severities (Sev A/B/C) are reported in the table; no fourth category exists in the source.
